summary: CBSSports.com previews Week 6 of the 2023 college football season using SportsLine consensus betting lines released Sunday. Four AP Top 25 matchups headline the slate: Texas-Oklahoma, Kentucky-Georgia, LSU-Missouri and Notre Dame-Louisville. The note also covers Alabama at Texas A&M and lists spreads for other notable games.
one_line: CBS Sports previews Week 6 of 2023 college football with SportsLine consensus odds for four ranked matchups, Alabama at Texas A&M, and other key games.
key_facts: The Red River Rivalry pits No. 3 Texas (-5.5) against No. 12 Oklahoma at the Cotton Bowl Stadium in Dallas; both are 5-0, the first time the rivals have met undefeated since 2011.
Texas and Oklahoma are the only undefeated and only ranked Big 12 teams, and both leave for the SEC in 2024; a two-loss team has never made the playoff.
No. 1 Georgia is a 15-point favorite over No. 20 Kentucky, Georgia's first ranked opponent of 2023; both teams are 5-0.
Georgia's two SEC wins this season both came from behind: at home against South Carolina in Week 3 and at Auburn in Week 5.
Kentucky running back Ray Davis rushed for 280 yards and three touchdowns in the Week 5 win against Florida, passing 200 yards well before halftime.
No. 23 LSU is a 6.5-point favorite at No. 21 Missouri; LSU has two losses, including a 55-49 defeat at Ole Miss in which it allowed 637 yards.
LSU allowed 426 yards in a 34-31 scare against Arkansas in Week 4.
Missouri quarterback Brady Cook ranks fourth in SEC passing with 1,468 yards, 11 touchdowns and no interceptions through five weeks.
No. 10 Notre Dame is a 6.5-point favorite at No. 25 Louisville, which is 5-0 in its first season under coach Jeff Brohm and is facing ranked competition for the first time in 2023.
Notre Dame lost to Ohio State in Week 4 and then won a comeback game at Duke in Week 5.
No. 11 Alabama is a 3.5-point favorite at Texas A&M; the Crimson Tide beat Ole Miss and Mississippi State by a combined 64-27.

Texas A&M beat top-ranked Alabama on a walk-off field goal at Kyle Field in 2021 and lost 24-20 at Bryant-Denny Stadium last year; Conner Weigman is out for the season, so former LSU transfer Max Johnson is making his second consecutive start.
Other lines include No. 2 Michigan (-20) at Minnesota, Virginia Tech at No. 5 Florida State (-25.5), and Maryland at No. 4 Ohio State (-18.5).
